convoLines.text: Nobody touches this group. Not while I'm standing.
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
It's quiet at the ridge. Blanca doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"I count heads at night. Every night. You get used to the arithmetic of care."
"Being the shield means you take the hits. I've made my peace with that."
"Still on what they want."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"
"Since Nancy died... I keep expecting to see Nancy at the fire. Stupid."
"I wish we had longer. Soon, yeah?"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Can we talk?" Hayden sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
They relax, a fraction. This is going well.
"Still on your read on people here. Told you."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Nancy is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I count portions out loud before eating. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
"Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful."
"Anger's a fire — useful if you cook with it, deadly if you sleep next to it. I cook with mine. Most days."
"Still on whether you're angry."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Cool, cool."
"Good question." "Nancy always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I keep turning over the last thing Nancy said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
You show them Wild Strawberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
Someone has to be the wall. I've got broad shoulders. Fine.
"Someone has to watch the treeline. I've appointed myself. No term limits."
"Protection looks boring when it works. I aim for boring."
"Like I said — Still on what they want."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Anyway — that's my cross to carry. What's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "I dreamed Nancy was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
You show them Wild Strawberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"About that question — What's something you're good at that nobody here knows about?"
"Noted. Filing that under 'extremely useful.' The village needs that."
The conversation cools to something businesslike.
"Still on what you're good at."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Nancy owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"I'm picking up Nancy's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
You show them Wild Strawberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "The Quiet Room. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"I do the small things right. The big things notice."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — What do you miss most? From before."
"God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"Look — Still on what you miss most."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "They took you — The Quiet Room, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."

"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."

"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"My part? I check everyone's shoes for wear and stay ready."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Good question." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I can't read, and I'm scared it matters now."
Issam has an edge today — something curdled.
"Watch for this: The grass stops moving the way wind moves it. Sweeps Week, every time. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on their secret."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
You show them Blackberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"...Anyway. What did you want to ask?"
"Good question." Someone has to be the memory of this place. I've volunteered.
"I should go. You know where to find me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
You know what you're doing. That's rare. That's good.
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Meet me at the meadow edge, west of the creek and we'll fill packs before dark."

d16: The village's quarrel was with Nancy — and Nancy is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
recoverHome: d17: That night, they bring Nancy home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.

d18: 📺 SYSTEM: "We have already cleared your morning. You are welcome. We require 300 kcal of tubers and your full attention. The fans love a cooking segment."
d18: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 67. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 5."
burialWindowSay: d16: The village's quarrel was with Nancy — and Nancy is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d17: That night, they bring Nancy home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d18: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+4 integration)
d19: You say a few words for Nancy. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d19: You bury Nancy. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
d19: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+3 integration)
echoSample: d19: "Since Nancy died... I keep expecting to see Nancy at the fire. Stupid."
d19: "Huh. Let me think about that." "Nancy is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
d19: "Good question." "Nancy always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
d19: "I keep turning over the last thing Nancy said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
d23: "You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "I dreamed Nancy was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
d23: "Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Nancy owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."

lastSay: d71: 🪞 You wake up somebody else. Hayden Song, 24 — a radio DJ. Their hands know different work now: Beast-calm, Scream Cheese, War Cry, Lucky Rock.
d71: The village's quarrel was with Dalila — and Dalila is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d71: You knew Dalila — not the office, the person. The fire keeps expecting her, and so do you. That's a heavier kind of stepping up. (+5 trauma)
d71: At the grave, Jada, Blanca, Issam and 6 more speak for Hayden — "Dalila trusted them. We saw it. Give them the fire's hearing." The village listens.
d71: The fire knew Hayden before the Codex did — their name already carried weight here.
